profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
DC1 occupies 22,000 square feet of technical space in a mid-rise office building at 1275 K St. NW, a form factor that signals a carrier-hotel or enterprise colocation role rather than a hyperscale or AI training deployment. No IT load figure in megawatts is published for this campus, so no translation into rack count or accelerator capacity is possible without inventing a number the operator has not provided. What can be said is that 22,000 square feet of raised-floor space is a modest footprint by any measure, and dense AI training workloads, which can consume 40 kW or more per rack, would fill that space with heat and power demand that a downtown urban building envelope typically cannot absorb at scale.

The certifications tell a clear story about the intended customer base. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the facility for tenants whose auditors require attested controls over financial and operational data. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for regulated health information. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 qualify it for tenants operating under information-security management frameworks, including federal agencies and their contractors. Together these six certifications describe a compliance-first facility aimed at regulated enterprise and government workloads, not at frontier model training.

This is the only facility this site has mapped in the District of Columbia, and no campus in DC has a published megawatt figure in this site's dataset, so no capacity ranking by power is possible within the state. DC1 ranks first by published megawatts only in the trivial sense that zero is equal across all mapped DC facilities. For a reader evaluating AI infrastructure, DC1 matters as a secure, compliance-heavy interconnection point for government-adjacent workloads, not as a compute concentration for large-scale model training or inference.
